(two real resting `TRAILING_STOP` BUYs left `get_account_balance` completely unchanged, so
`notional_cap`/the cash check can't stop a second BUY once the first has filled — the existing
resting-order dup guards only cover the window before a fill). New
`tests/test_fake_broker_buy_blocked_position_exists_scenario.py` (2 scenarios). Fixing this surfaced
5 pre-existing `test_schwab_safety.py` tests that were seeding a leftover open position before an
unrelated BUY call meant to test cap/burst-cap logic in isolation — fixed by reordering each test's
`_seed_position()` call and adding a `_clear_position()` helper (raw DELETE, not `close_position()`,
to avoid tripping `same_day_block` for the cash-type `ira` account).

**Fix 2 — TRAIL-exit reminder spam.** Investigated the older 2026-07-28 GDXU backlog item (3

## 2026-08-03 (later) — FFT/rhythm-for-entry-timing research thread: methodology mismatch caught by review, pivoted to time-of-day, found a real-but-mixed effect, then walk-forward-validated it down to 2 real candidates

Started from "can FFT help identify signals better" — aimed first at explaining the empirically-chosen
`window` parameter (10 vs 20). Built `scripts/fft_cycle_analysis.py`, found no significant spectral
cycle in any of the 10 v5 watchlist tickers' returns (permutation-null p=0.076-0.837). Had an
independent Opus review the methodology before trusting the negative result — it confirmed no bug,
proved the pipeline works (found the real, known 3.5-bar intraday volatility seasonality as a
positive control), but flagged the real problem: a rolling z-score exploits mean-reversion *speed*,
not periodicity, so FFT peak-hunting was structurally incapable of answering the original question
either way. Logged as refuted (for the tested framing) in `docs/research_log.md`, backlog updated.

User then asked a different, sharper question: can rhythm decide entry timing directly? Tested two
framings, both negative even after applying the review's fixes (Welch's method, block-bootstrap null
instead of the anti-conservative iid-shuffle one, targeted multi-day band) — no v5 ticker shows a
real repeating price wave (`scripts/multiday_cycle_entry_test.py`).

Pivoted to a non-FFT idea instead: does the *time of day* a signal fires matter (live trading treats
the 9:30 and 14:30 daily signal windows as equally trustworthy, never tested)? `scripts/
entry_timing_seasonality.py` on the 10 v5 tickers found nothing significant — but the user correctly
flagged a selection-bias concern (these 10 already survived a resweep for overall alpha, and their
params were already optimized, potentially absorbing any such effect). Re-ran against the broader
18-ticker v4 universe (`--watchlist-id 57`, added as a flag rather than a new script) and found a
real, statistically significant pooled effect (p<0.0001) with 6 individual tickers flagged, mixed
direction (some tickers prefer morning, some afternoon) — not a universal rule.

Chased one side-thread: UVIX's afternoon trades were net losers on average — checked whether that
was a stock-split/data artifact (it wasn't; UVIX genuinely decayed ~150x over 3 years, real
structural volatility-ETF decay, confirmed via a raw bar-by-bar >15%-move scan) and confirmed
removing UVIX doesn't change the pooled significance. Also ruled out one hypothesis
directly: does price systematically fall through the day, explaining why the 14:30 window fires ~3x
more BUY signals than 9:30? No — `scripts/intraday_drift_check.py` found no real net drift (mean
+0.048%, essentially a coin flip); that volume imbalance is unexplained, likely just cumulative
opportunity by the later bar, not investigated further.

Finished with a walk-forward validation (`scripts/entry_timing_walkforward_check.py`, chronological
2-fold split, same convention as the existing `walk_forward_check.py`) on the 3 strongest candidates
(GDXD, UVIX, DPST). GDXD and UVIX's morning-preference holds up consistently in both halves — real,
validated findings. DPST's does NOT hold up (reverses direction in the second half) — correctly
caught before it could have been mistakenly applied to DPST's real live-money node. Net actionable
result: **nothing changes in live trading today** — GDXD/UVIX are research-mode-only, not live, and
DPST's version of the effect didn't survive validation. Parked as a validated-but-not-yet-actionable
finding for future work (e.g. if either ticker is ever promoted, or as a check to run on future
candidates). Full detail in `docs/research_log.md`'s six 2026-08-03 entries; open items in
`docs/backlog_cache.md` (signal-volume-imbalance mechanism still unexplained).

**Housekeeping**: 5 new research scripts this session (`fft_cycle_analysis.py`,
`entry_timing_seasonality.py`, `multiday_cycle_entry_test.py`, `intraday_drift_check.py`,
`entry_timing_walkforward_check.py`), plus the FFT-cycle-detection backlog item closed and its

if asked).

## 2026-08-03 (later still) — Paired-ticker capital allocation research: idle-capital reuse tested and superseded by a concurrent/additive hedge framing

Picked up from the earlier FFT/rhythm session close. User proposed using a ticker's real matched
leveraged inverse (SOXL/SOXS, QID/QLD, GDXU/GDXD, etc.) to put idle capital to work while a primary
v5 node's position is closed.

**Static holding, rejected**: `scripts/sim_v6_inverse_parking.py` held the inverse for the whole idle
window — wrecked by leveraged-ETF decay on rare month-plus gaps (GDXD -87% compounded despite a 65%
per-window win rate). Not what the user meant anyway once clarified: they wanted the inverse actively
traded on its own signal rules, only during idle time.

**Idle-capital multiplier framing**: built 3 variants — strict zero-overlap (`sim_v6_inverse_secondary_trade.py`),
forced-exit-on-primary-reentry (`sim_constrained_inverse_pair.py`), and aggressive-flip
(`sim_paired_flip_strategy.py`, has a bug fixed mid-session but not yet cleanly rerun end-to-end).
Widened the candidate pool beyond true inverse pairs per the user's "we just want filler" note
(`sim_v6_filler_scan.py`, 12-ticker pool). Built a real joint-capital merge (`sim_v6_joint_capital.py`)
that compounds primary's own trades + filler's non-overlapping trades into one chronological curve,
tested both role assignments (which ticker is primary vs. filler) per the user's own suggestion.
Real results: AGQ-primary/ZSL-filler is the standout (1.56x multiplier on total compounded gain);
GDXU/GDXD works both directions (1.09x/1.27x); NUGT/DUST fails either way (DUST has no cliff-safe
node at any fixed_sl, win rates 0.5-14%). Ran a live (non-cached) grid search for SOXS since it had
zero v5 data, found a reasonably clustered node (w20/z1.5/sl2), but SOXL/SOXS failed both directions
(0.51x/0.97x) — traced to a real ~11.6% weekend gap in the underlying that SOXL had already exited
before, so SOXS's matching loss had no concurrent SOXL gain to offset it.

That SOXL/SOXS trace became the pivot: the idle-capital-multiplier framing is NOT a hedge — primary
and filler never overlap in time by construction, so a bad filler loss during a real gap event is
never cushioned by a concurrent primary gain. User confirmed they actually want an **additive/
concurrent** structure instead: both legs funded and held simultaneously (separate capital, not idle
reuse), sized close to balanced rather than skewed toward one side (the "11×2 < 5×5" square-maximizes-
area intuition — worth confirming the optimal split empirically, not assuming 50/50). Explicitly not
a v5 variant; needs its own version tag once built for real.

Also resolved a side question: KORU's historical real inverse (KORZ, Direxion Daily South Korea Bear)
is delisted — confirmed via yfinance, no live pairing available for that ticker.

**Status**: no concurrent-capital backtest built yet — this is real design/build work queued for next
session, not something to prototype further ad hoc. Full detail in `docs/deep_backlog.md`'s 2026-08-03
(paired-capital) entry; short pointer in `docs/backlog_cache.md`.

**Housekeeping**: 6 new research scripts this session (`sim_v6_inverse_parking.py`,

## 2026-08-03 (evening) — Pairs paradigm decisively refuted via a 90-pair matrix; HIBL/USD/YANG go live with real funding; SOXS added to v5; USO found as a 1x standout

Picked up from the earlier paired-capital session close. Ran the SOXL/GDXU/AGQ/NUGT idle-capital-multiplier
framing further, then the user challenged the whole premise: is this different from just running two
uncorrelated nodes? Agreed to test it properly rather than keep tuning.

**The decisive test**: `/tmp/all_v5_pairs.py` computed the joint-capital multiplier for all 90 directional
pairs among the 10 real v5 watchlist tickers (no inverse relationship needed at all). Result: mean 1.02,
median 0.96, spread 0.27x-3.45x, 40/90 help vs 38/90 hurt — centered at "no effect," more variance than
any of the "special" inverse pairs. 7 of the top 12 "mutually beneficial" pairs involved GDXU specifically,
traced to its small standalone-return denominator mechanically amplifying ratio noise, not a real pairing
property. Time-sliced SOXL/GDXU/AGQ/NUGT into 5 equal calendar periods to test luck-vs-consistency directly:
most "1.0x" cells were literally zero-fit periods (no real interaction, not neutral); the one pair with real
fits across all 5 periods (SOXL/AGQ) was consistently a mild *drag* (0.72-1.09x), the only genuinely
time-consistent result found all session — and it's negative. SOXS's earlier 1.85x headline number traced to
an n=2 real-period sample that didn't even agree with itself (2.10x then 0.74x), though verified the two
sub-period multipliers do compose multiplicatively into the full-period figure.

**Verdict: pairs paradigm closed.** No coordination mechanism between tickers showed a reliable payoff,
inverse or otherwise — practical conclusion is to keep running nodes independently, as the live watchlist
already does. Individual nodes' own backtested edges are unaffected; only the *combination* mechanism was
refuted. Full writeup: `docs/research_log.md`'s two 2026-08-03 entries (pairs refutation + 1x universe screen).

**Side investigations same session**: explained why DUST/ZSL/SOXS underperform standalone (-94% to -96.5%
buy-and-hold — daily-reset leveraged decay against a strong secular bull in the underlying, same mechanism
across gold miners/silver/semis) vs. their bullish twins (NUGT +65%, AGQ +111%, SOXL +367%). Screened 30
non-leveraged 1x tickers (sector/index/commodity/international ETFs) for a cleaner mean-reversion candidate
without the leveraged-decay confound — found **USO** (1x crude oil) as a real standout: +105.9% alpha vs SPY,
52.2% win rate, 67 trades, robust across window 5-10 in a follow-up sensitivity check. Everything else in the
1x screen came back negative alpha (too low-volatility for the z-score dislocation to trigger meaningfully).
Not yet run through a real committed v5 sweep — flagged in `docs/backlog_cache.md`.

**User ran the real SOXS v5 sweep to completion this session** (`run_sweep_queue.sh`, both strategies,
`fixed_sl∈{1,2,3}`): `TrailingBothZScoreBreakout` has no cliff-safe node at any `fixed_sl` (an earlier

## 2026-08-04 — Portfolio de-risking marathon: bear-market simulation suite built, AGQ's K-1/UBTI status discovered and reverses its account placement, USO/AGQ both blocked from IRA at the code level

Started from a portfolio-management question (de-risk given the rest of the portfolio is already
aggressive; should profits get skimmed into SPY ahead of a downturn) and ran the full session on it —
no kernel/strategy code touched until the very end.

**Bear-market stress-test suite built from scratch** (`scripts/sim_bear_market_stress.py` and five
follow-on scripts): synthetic daily-bar leveraged-ETF reconstruction from long-history 1x underlyings
(since real hourly cache only goes back ~2-3 years, no real crash coverage) against 2008 GFC/2020
COVID/2022 bear windows. Strategy protects hard on the way down vs buy-and-hold, but gives back most
of the recovery leg — full-cycle combined verdict still favors the strategy in most cases (10/12 GFC,
9/12 2022, mixed 6/12 COVID), so "stop and hold long" during a crash is not supported by the data.

**Skim-and-reserve "insurance policy" overlay designed and real-tested** (`sim_skim_redeploy.py`,
`sim_real_skim_reserve.py`, `sim_downturn_reinvest_vs_hold.py`, `sim_double_policy_multi.py`): landed
on automated skim (10% new-high step / 20% fraction ratchet into SPY, day-1 activation) + manual
redeploy (alert at both 80%/100% recovery, no universal best threshold found). A real bug was found
and fixed mid-session — the "double" redeploy trigger initially fired on day 1 for every ticker
(pre-decline flat bars trivially satisfied the recovery check), inflating early results; fixed with a
has-declined-first gate. Broad multi-ticker/multi-reserve testing (SPY/QQQ/SSO/UPRO/QLD/TQQQ) found no
reserve universally beats plain "hold" once the trigger is standardized — SOXL and AGQ are the two
tickers where the mechanism clearly helps. Design spec'd in full but not implemented (no real capital
deployed yet, user extending paper-trading validation deliberately).

**Real year-by-year backtests** (not just multi-year aggregates) found a strong regime effect: SOXL
strategy +84% (2024)/+492% (2025)/-40.8% (2026 YTD) vs buy-and-hold -5%/+49%/+142.8% same years — the
strategy wins in choppy years, loses badly in trending ones, confirmed independently on SSO too
(+47%/+41%/-0.4% vs +44%/+25%/+16%). Four separate attempts to find a predictive/regime signal (200-day
z-score bucketing, monthly-return autocorrelation, seasonal/quarterly splits) all came back negative or
too-thin-to-trust — no way found to know in advance which regime is coming.

**Real out-of-sample check on SOXL** (`sim_out_of_sample_check.py`): a 50/50 chronological split
independently re-derived the exact params already live in production, and the held-out test half still
returned +173.5% (vs +305% in-sample) — real decay from overfitting, but not "no edge," confirming the
backtested edge is directionally genuine.

**Major finding, discovered very late in the session: AGQ is a K-1/Section 1256 commodity pool**
(confirmed via ProShares' own tax documentation), not a standard '40-Act fund like SOXL. This means (a)
AGQ carries real UBTI/Form 990-T exposure if held in an IRA/Roth/SEP (custodian debits the tax directly
from IRA assets, automatically, once gross K-1 income crosses $1,000/year — very plausible given real
trading activity), and (b) AGQ is *exempt* from the wash-sale rule and gets a favorable 60/40
blended tax rate in a *taxable* account instead — the exact opposite of SOXL, and the opposite of what
this session concluded earlier in the night. This reverses the account-placement plan: **SOXL → IRA/Roth,
AGQ → brokerage** (not both to IRA/Roth as originally concluded). The earlier `sim_wash_sale_impact.py`
AGQ numbers are wrong/superseded (real corrected AGQ 2026 YTD after-tax: +68.3%, not +57.7%, with zero
wash-sale carry-forward drag). SOXL's wash-sale result stands unchanged. Checked the rest of the
watchlist for the same blind spot: NUGT/JNUG/JDST (Direxion, confirmed RIC/1099, no K-1) and GDXU
(MicroSectors ETN, different structure, no K-1) are both clean — AGQ is the one real outlier, not a
sign of a broader pattern.

## 2026-08-04 (very late) — AGQ/SOXL 2026 divergence investigation, drought-overlay/put-hedge design, live config-drift gap found and fixed, paper-vs-backtest reconciliation opens a real architecture problem

Pivoted from portfolio-construction planning into a long research/tooling session after the user

**AGQ/SOXL 2026 divergence, six research passes**: breach velocity, chop-cluster persistence, a
regime regression (vol/slope/z-crossing-rate/z-saturation), a config cross-apply test, and a
near-miss retracement test all came back negative or non-explanatory. The real mechanism, found via
`scripts/period_volatility_regression.py` then decisively corrected after the user caught it as a
frequency artifact (more trades != better trades, verified via decomposition): AGQ's 2026 gain came
almost entirely from one violent 3-week crash (Feb 2026, real -48% single day, no data-integrity
issue); SOXL's weak 2026 comes from a genuine 6-week smooth rally the strategy structurally can't
trade (zero signals fired the whole stretch) -- not a bug, the mean-reversion trigger needs
volatility to fire at all.

**Drought-overlay design and testing**: since the real lever is signal frequency not quality
(retuning the z-threshold would be single-episode curve-fitting), designed and tested a "buy the
underlying after a confirmed quiet stretch, manage with the core strategy's own arm-then-trail exit
mechanics" overlay (`scripts/drought_overlay_test.py`). Result: mechanistically sound but not
validated -- SOXL's positive result (+30% compounded) is driven by 2 of 13 trades, fragile; pooled
result across the 10 v5 tickers still net negative. Real finding: gap-through-SL risk is
concentrated in volatile/idiosyncratic leveraged sector-commodity names (KORU/AGQ/YANG, max excess
30.6%) vs. broad-index leveraged funds (SPY/QQQ family, max excess 2.0%) -- a real, useful
underlying-specific safety split. Put-hedge identified as the structural fix for gap risk (can't be
gapped through, unlike a stop), with a real tailwind (IV tends to be cheap exactly when the drought
detector would fire) -- not backtestable (no historical options data anywhere accessible).
`scripts/drought_detection_test.py` (a twice-daily vol-percentile read) found ~zero advance warning a
drought is starting, ~50% hit rate for warning one is ending.

## 2026-08-05 (very late) — Daily-track paper trading built and thoroughly corrected: pure-observation reconcile classifier (not resync-and-halt), 3 full paired-review rounds, 2 real live-check bugs closed

Session's main thread: a second `watch_list` paper node per v5-watchlist ticker
(`paper_role='daily_sync'`, "daily-track") alongside the existing free-running "live-track", isolating
whether paper trading's price source (live tick vs. backtest's hourly-bar Close) explains its
divergence from a backtest replay. `signals_compute.compute_buy_signal` gained a `daily_sync` branch
forcing signal-check pricing to the last closed hourly bar's Close (with a staleness guard and a fix
for yfinance's still-forming current-hour bar).

**The design went through a real reversal, driven entirely by user pushback, not a bug report.** The
first working version was a "reconcile-and-resync" engine (`paper_trading.reconcile_daily_track_nodes`,
nightly EOD job): it auto-opened/closed daily-track's paper positions whenever a divergence from the
backtest was proven explained by price, and halted a node's future entries when it couldn't explain
one. After it was built and reviewed twice, the user reconsidered the whole premise: "i'm not sure i
agree with halts... in fact letting it run might show up more interesting behaviors" → "no i think i
didn't want to auto sync" → final framing, "reconcile as one action (how far are we) vs sync (prepare
for next day)". Reasoning: auto-resyncing erases exactly the natural divergence that's most
interesting to study over a long comparison window; auto-halting quiets a node down exactly when
something is happening. The function was rewritten to be pure observation — it still runs the full
comparison/counterfactual logic (bar-level entry match, exit-bar match, "would Close alone explain
this" checks for entry misses and both SL and trailing-stop exit wicks) but never calls
`open_position`/`close_position`/`set_daily_sync_halted`; it only classifies and logs one full
diagnostic row per node per night to a new `daily_track_reconciliation_log` table. The
`daily_sync_halted_at` schema/gate/invariant-check were deliberately left in place, inert, as
scaffolding for a possible future separate "sync" tool.

**Three full paired Opus review rounds (independent-cold + contextual), each against a real diff, each
finding real bugs** — this is also why `CLAUDE.md`'s `session wrap` step 3a was rewritten this session
to explicitly require the pair (it previously said "spawn an independent Opus review agent," singular,
which the user caught mid-session: "why did you forget?" — the paired pattern lived only in a memory
note, not in CLAUDE.md itself). Round 1 found the original reconcile-and-resync engine's nightly reset
would force-close every position before it could ever complete a real multi-day trade (all v5 nodes
have `max_hold_hours` 21-140h) — this is what triggered the pure-observation redesign discussion.
Round 2 found the `'closed'` state permanently shadowed `'flat'` once a node had any trade history
(fixed by anchoring the comparison on the backtest's own most recent trade instead of daily-track's);
a real trailing-buy fill's `signal_time` is deliberately wall-clock, unresolvable to a bar index
(fixed via a new `signal_bar_time` column); bar-close exits were off-by-one (fixed via a parallel
`exit_bar_time` column); a `numpy.bool_` identity-comparison bug. Round 3 (on the final
pure-observation design plus a new trailing-stop wick counterfactual, `_close_alone_would_breach_trail`)
found an unarmed TIME-forced exit was misclassified as an explained SL wick — and the independent
review found the deeper root cause: `scripts/export_trades.py::simulate_trail_exit_chaos` never
tracked `arm_i` at all for the `TrailingExitZScoreBreakout` kernel mirror, silently misrouting every
genuine trailing-stop exit for that whole strategy family. Fixed at the source (verified no other of
its 13 consumer scripts reads the field). Also fixed: a documented-but-never-emitted `no_backtest_data`
action, silent replay failures, several stale resync/halt-era comments, and 4 test assertions
strengthened from `is not None` to exact value checks.

Separately, two real live-check bugs from a prior session's finding were closed:
`get_pending_buys_for_ticker_on_date`'s exact-date match (broke `canary_overnight_carry` for SDOW/DIA)
fixed to `<=`, and `audit_one`/`status_check.py` never checking `pending_buys` (a resting trailing-buy
showed as "flat") fixed via new `get_pending_buy_by_wl_id`. A cosmetic stale status-message time string
from the same finding remains open.

Full suite: 539 passed, 0 errors (also incidentally cleared 1 pre-existing unrelated collection error —
`scripts/multiday_cycle_entry_test.py`'s `test_ticker_cycle` helper, not a real pytest test, renamed to
`analyze_ticker_cycle`). Test coverage: `tests/test_daily_track_paper.py` (30 tests, zero
state-mutation assertions by design), `tests/test_export_trades_arm_tracking.py` (4 new tests).

**Not done**: no daily-track node created against the real live DB yet
(`scripts/add_daily_track_paper_nodes.py` built/tested, confirm before running); piece 4
(`scripts/paper_vs_backtest_reconcile.py`'s own rebuild) and the kernel's "waiting"/bounce-fill state
visibility remain open, lower priority.

## 2026-08-05 (very late 3) — Drought-overlay deep dive: intraday vol entry-gate found (real but ticker-dependent, unresolved overfitting risk), exit-side vol-spike rule tested and rejected, HANDOFF mechanism traced, per-ticker 5-axis sweep built

Continuation of the SOXL-only drought-overlay fragility question. User asked for a much bigger
sample first (widened to the 18-ticker v4 universe + a new `--big6` broad-index mode in
`scripts/drought_overlay_sweep.py`), then a manual trade-by-trade audit of SOXL's specific
losses, which led into a real methodological finding: **daily-close 5-day realized vol
systematically masks intraday volatility** (it only samples 5 closes) -- rebuilding the vol
measure as rolling stdev of hourly log returns, with the 9:30 bar excluded (a near-instantaneous
overnight repricing, not accumulated intraday trading activity), sharpened the entry-side
win-rate split from 57%/33% to a much cleaner 60%/14% (low-vol vs high-vol entries) across all 26
real HANDOFF-exit trades. A parallel "declining vs rising drift during the drought" hypothesis
was tested and found to add nothing on top (correlation ~0, vol doing all the discriminating
work) -- underpowered sample caveat noted (only 5/26 droughts were declining).

**Exit-side vol-spike rule tested and rejected**: exiting early when intraday vol spikes while
underwater looked great on SOXL's 4 example trades (both real losses cut ~4x smaller) but broke
badly at scale -- run across all 313 real drought windows, it also guillotined 9 trades that were
going to be big TRAIL wins (+3.6% to +34.9%, cut to -0.15% to -2.5%), since the rule can't tell a
capitulation dip before a recovery from the start of a real decline. Net: compounded improved
(-92.7% -> -78.8%) but win rate got worse (14.7% -> 11.5%). **Do not adopt as designed.**

**HANDOFF mechanism traced**: sells at the backstop bar's Open unconditionally once neither SL nor
trail has fired. Checked whether it systematically sells right before the core strategy's own
trade rallies (the intuitive worst-timing story) -- only 2/14 HANDOFF losses (14%) actually show
that pattern; the dominant shape (12/14) is correlated continuation (the core trade's own next
signal also loses). SOXL's 2025-10-22 trade is the one real "sold right before the recovery" case
(overlay exited at 36.78, core trade rallied +31.4% to 49.89).

**AGQ margin-funded add-on-at-arm — validated.** Original entry: 41 armed trades, 0 losses (structural, arm=8% >> trail=7%, confirmed this "can't lose once armed" property holds for 7/10 v5 tickers but not NUGT/UDOW/YANG where trail% exceeds arm%). Add-on leg (buy more at arm, margin-funded): 54% win rate, +3.55%/event, +247.5% compounded across all 41 events. Cliff-safety-checked across a real arm%/trail% neighborhood — smooth, not a lucky peak. Margin cost negligible (~0.03-0.05% of borrowed amount for a typical ~33h hold). Real full 24-ticker (18-ticker v4 + big6) three-layer (core/overlay/add-on) comparison table built via `scripts/three_layer_summary.py`.

**Real prune bug found and root-caused.** All 18 v4-watchlist tickers' `TrailingBoth` v5 backtest_cache data is silently zero (0 rows) in the current pruned DB — real data existed pre-prune (SOXL alone had 838K rows, real robust_alpha up to 1212.1%), confirmed intact in the permanent pre-prune archive. Root cause: `prune_backtest_cache.py`'s island-selection SQL filters `take_profit IN (?)`, but `TrailingBoth` stores its arm value in `arm_sell_pct`, leaving `take_profit` NULL for every row — SQL's `IN (NULL)` matches nothing, silently dropping the entire strategy for every v4-universe ticker. Big-6 tickers' `TrailingBoth` data survived only because it was computed 2026-08-03, the day *after* the prune ran — not a real survivor. **Not yet fixed** — flagged, not resolved this session.

**Put-hedge deep dive on the core strategy's own positions (not just the drought-overlay).** Long iterative back-and-forth correcting real modeling errors along the way (documented in `docs/research_log.md`'s 2026-08-06 entries, not fully re-summarized here): wrong per-night decay reference (nearest/steepest-curve option instead of a longer-dated flatter one), wrong strike altitude (5% OTM is redundant with the existing 2-3% SL and too far to be cheap tail insurance), wrong ATM-IV lookup (grabbed a non-ATM strike, inflating IV 2x). Corrected model: 15%/25%/50%-OTM puts, real ATM IV, Black-Scholes-priced, tested against 4 real historical crash reconstructions (`scripts/sim_bear_market_stress.py` — 2008 GFC, 2020 COVID, 2022 bear, 2000 dotcom synthetic daily-bar leveraged-ETF price paths, pre-existing tool from an earlier session).

**Real, final result: SOXL benefits from the hedge at every OTM level (15/25/50%) and every crash tested — a genuine, consistent positive** (e.g., +23.1pp better at 15% OTM in 2000 dotcom). **KORU's hedge costs more than it saves in its two worst crashes (2008 GFC, 2022 bear) at every strike tested** (e.g., -18.6pp at 15% OTM in 2008 GFC), though the cost shrinks going further OTM. Root cause: KORU's real IV is extreme (234%, vs SOXL's 180%) — a 15%-OTM put costs 13.2% of spot per 20-day cycle at that vol vs. essentially nothing at "normal" 30% IV; real bear markets are a long grind with real relief rallies, and a put loses heavily on those rallies (theta + delta), taxing exactly the recoveries the equity curve needs to climb out of drawdown. Also confirmed a genuine ruin-protection argument distinct from average cost/benefit: even where the hedge costs money on average (KORU), it still caps a true-wipeout scenario (synthetic crash bottoms found the underlying can implode -80% to -99.6%) at roughly the OTM strike distance instead of -100% — a categorically different, asymmetric kind of value the pp-gain tables don't capture.

**Two new backlog items logged**, both scoped and ready to pick up: (1) emergency-procedures runbook — no real-time crash-detection trigger exists anywhere in this system (everything tested tonight used retrospectively-known crash windows), and no human runbook distinct from the existing kill-switch; real fund-closure/delisting risk is also unmodeled. Also open: whether SOXL needs skim-and-reserve *in addition to* the now-validated put hedge (different jobs, never tested combined).

Executed `docs/design.md`'s 2026-08-07 staged checklist for two of the three planned mechanisms plus drought overlay (put-hedge explicitly excluded, user's call at session start): DB schema → DB functions → paper-trading logic → daily-track sync → nightly reconcile → Accountability Grid rows → truth-table tests → live daemon wiring. Full detail: `docs/deep_backlog.md`'s 2026-08-09 entry (top), `docs/design.md`'s new addendum at the end of the file.

**Four rounds of paired Opus review** (independent-cold + contextual each, three fully paired, the final contextual retry hit four consecutive server-side 529 overloads and was not completed — proceeded on the strength of the successful independent-cold pass plus two earlier successful contextual reviews mid-session) found and fixed a combined 1 CRITICAL + 5 HIGH + many MEDIUM/LOW real bugs, every one individually re-verified with a new or updated test before moving on:

1. **[CRITICAL]** `check_paper_drought_handoff` checked `sig is None` instead of `sig['signal'] == 'BUY'` — `compute_buy_signal` returns a real dict (`signal='HOLD'`) on almost every poll, never `None` just because there's no signal. Would have closed every drought position on nearly every poll inside a signal window, permanently starving every gap (once-per-gap guard compounds it).
2. **[HIGH]** Drought entry re-entered unboundedly within one gap — fixed via a `drought_gap_start`-keyed dedup.
3. **[HIGH]** HANDOFF-before-core-scan ordering was violated by a third real core-entry path, `_scan_pinned_entry` — the actual primary mechanism for every real drought candidate. Fixed by adding HANDOFF inside the pinned-bar loop too (with a matching entry_timing/AUTOMATION_ENABLED_TICKERS filter, added in a follow-up fix after an initial version had no filter at all), plus refreshing the stale `open_position_keys` snapshot afterward.
4. **[HIGH]** Redeploy alert fired against a genuinely empty reserve — missing the reference's `w_spy > 0` guard (an independent review's differential simulation over 500 random equity paths proved this one guard explained 100% of the divergence).
5. **[HIGH]** Skim amount formula diverged from the validated model in the wrong direction — first fixed to stop recomputing off the full undiluted notional, but that fix over-corrected: `strategy_value` then only ever shrank via skims, never grew by the strategy's own realized returns. Fixed by compounding it with the just-closed trade's own return before each skim check.
6. **[HIGH]** Skim state (`skim_ref`/`peak`/`min_since_peak`/`strategy_value`) seeded at a flat `1.0`/`starting_notional` baseline regardless of a node's real accumulated equity — enabling skim on a node with real prior paper-trading history would fire one false giant skim capturing the entire pre-existing gain in a single shot. Fixed by seeding from the node's actual current equity on its first-ever `check_paper_skim` call (which fires no skim itself).
7. Plus: vol-gate `None`-polarity inversion, missing `mode='live'` guard, no fault isolation in the nightly reconcile, an unmemoized per-poll CSV re-read, missing `node['arm_pct']`/`node['z']` normalization in the reconcile replay (found only once it ran against real cached data), the ambient window gate not accounting for `_ambient_buy_scan_nodes`' own `:25-:29` pre-pinned exclusion (fixed by reusing that function's real output directly instead of re-deriving an approximation), `INSERT OR IGNORE` letting a transient replay failure permanently mask a later clean reconcile result (switched to `INSERT OR REPLACE`), and several stale "not wired" docstrings/comments corrected after the wiring actually landed.

**Known, documented (not silently glossed) limitation**: `reconcile_overlay_nodes` compares each mechanism's backtest replay against a node's *entire* cached price history, with no anchor to when the mechanism was actually enabled — for a node enabled mid-history this can produce a persistent, not-self-resolving false divergence in the nightly log. The *live mechanism's own behavior* is correct (confirmed by the seeding fix above), only the reconcile *comparison* has this gap. A real fix needs a persisted "enabled_at" timestamp — deferred as real schema work rather than rushed at session-wrap.

**Blast radius**: everything built is paper-only. No path from any new function reaches `schwab_client`/`schwab_safety` (traced explicitly across all four review rounds). The real live DB (`trading_live.db`) was never migrated this session — `ensure_tables()` only ever run against copies; the schema lands automatically the next daemon restart. Every new config flag defaults to `0`/`NULL`, so this is a genuine no-op for the current real watchlist until a node is deliberately opted in.

**Verification**: 27 new tests (`tests/test_overlay_paper_trading.py`), full suite 566 passed (was 539 at session start), `scripts/live_sim_harness.py` 7/7, `scripts/verify_trailing_buy_resolution.py`/`verify_trailing_sell_resolution.py --tickers AGQ,SOXL` clean (required since `active_signals.py` changed), `signals_invariants.py` clean against the real live DB, `check_backlog_cache_lean.py` clean.

## 2026-08-1x (later same day) — Real drought-entry/add-on-entry order-placement code built end-to-end; paired Opus review found and fixed 2 CRITICAL + 4 HIGH + 2 MEDIUM real defects, all re-verified with fake_broker tests reproducing the real call ordering

Picked up the session's own open "real-order execution edit plan" (`docs/plans/real_order_execution_drought_addon.md`) — implemented all 9 build phases: DB schema (`pending_buys`/`addon_legs` real-order columns), `schwab_safety`/`schwab_client`'s new `is_addon_leg` exemption, real drought-overlay entry (`signals_notify.check_drought_entry`/`notify_drought_buy_signal`, sharing `paper_trading.evaluate_drought_entry`'s eligibility logic with paper), real drought HANDOFF (`check_drought_handoff`, the new cancel-race/unconfirmed-exit state machine paper never has), real margin add-on entry (`check_addon_trigger_real`, triggered from `notify_trailing_activated`'s tail) and its lockstep close (`close_addon_leg_real_if_open`, wired into all 7 real exit call sites), 8 new Accountability Grid rows, reconciliation extended to `mode='live'` nodes, and 22 new fake_broker scenario tests across 4 new files.

**D1-D6 resolved**: D1/D2/D3 adopted the plan's own recommendations (`is_addon_leg` flag, buying-power check with 2.0x headroom, leg's own stop anchored to the parent's entry price). D3 required an unplanned extension the plan didn't spell out — a SELL-side `is_addon_leg` exemption, since the leg's own stop collides with `check_order`'s existing resting-SELL duplicate guard. D4 (drought sizing) confirmed by reading `generate_drought_trades` directly — it's sizing-agnostic, so paper's flat `starting_notional` convention carries over unchanged. D5 (combined core+addon exposure vs. `soxl_ira`'s cap) deliberately NOT a new invented number — implemented as `core_notional + addon_notional <= account.notional_cap`, reusing the existing cap conservatively rather than picking an arbitrary multiplier. D6 (first staged-test node) explicitly left for the user — no agent step flips a node live.

**Paired independent-cold + contextual Opus review, both converged on the same root defect**: the lockstep leg-exit SELL was structurally unplaceable at all 7 real call sites, because `db.close_position()` always runs (and deletes the parent's `open_positions` row) before the leg's own close attempt, and `check_order`'s SELL-branch preconditions were parent-position-scoped. Fixed architecturally — the `is_addon_leg` SELL exemption (and its size bound) now resolves the leg via a node-scoped lookup (`get_open_addon_leg_by_wl_id`), valid regardless of whether the parent row still exists, rather than reordering any of the 7 call sites. A second CRITICAL (cold review): once the leg's own stop was resting, the PARENT's own ordinary exit was blocked by seeing the leg's stop as a duplicate SELL — fixed via a plural `exclude_order_ids` on `_has_open_sell_order`, always excluding a known leg's `sl_order_id` regardless of `is_addon_leg`.

**Two more real bugs in the same surface were found only by test-driven verification, not by either review**: writing a fake_broker test that faithfully reproduced the real call-site ordering (`db.close_position()` first, `close_addon_leg_real_if_open()` second) surfaced that `check_order`'s separate duplicate-order-*fingerprint* check (account/ticker/side/quantity within a 60s window — distinct from the resting-order guard) also collided in both directions: the leg's own stop looked like a fingerprint-dup of the parent's just-placed arm-time SELL, and the parent's later real exit looked like a fingerprint-dup of the leg's own recently-placed stop, since leg and core shares are identical by construction. Fixed by skipping this check for SELL whenever the node has any open addon leg, not just when the current call is the leg's own placement.

**4 more HIGH findings fixed**: no dry-run fill synthesis for the leg (contextual review) — a `dry_run=True` account (the plan's own mandatory rehearsal prerequisite) produced no real order-id, permanently stranding the leg on both entry and exit; fixed by detecting a genuine dry-run no-op (`(None, None)` without a raise) and synthesizing the fill/close immediately, mirroring `update_dry_run_buys`'s existing convention. An unconfirmed entry fill left the leg with no stop ever placed (cold review) — fixed by adding the stop-placement call to the reconciliation sweep's late-fill branch. `set_addon_leg_exit_order_id` existed but was called nowhere, so an unconfirmed exit SELL had zero further tracking (cold review) — fixed by persisting the order id and adding a third reconciliation check that polls and closes it later. Plus 2 MEDIUM fixes (a dry-run leg falsely recording `broker_stop_price`; the manual "Filled" modal's share prefill not being drought-aware, inconsistent with the sibling fix already applied to `handle_entry_price`).

**Not fixed, explicitly deferred**: the orphaned-leg reconciliation alert has no throttle (same failure shape as the 2026-08-02 TRAIL-reminder spam, narrower window now given the fixes above); the leg's own stop firing independently of the parent is undetected (D3's own plan language already accepts this as a known gap); the full `test_fake_broker_overlay_truth_table_scenario.py` file from the plan's Part 9 list was not written (the four files that were written already drove and proved the real code, including finding the bugs above).

**Blast radius**: nothing flipped live. Every mechanism still defaults off (0/NULL) for every real node; migration verified idempotent against a copy of `trading_live.db`, not applied to the real one in-session. Full suite: 589/590 passed (1 pre-existing environmental failure — `test_automated_exit_sell_replace_updates_stale_sl_order_id`'s `webbrowser.Error`, confirmed unrelated to this diff, reproduces identically in isolation and on the pre-diff tree). `scripts/live_sim_harness.py`: 7/7. `signals_invariants.py`: clean, including a new `check_addon_drought_live_nodes_have_coherent_account_type` check. `scripts/check_backlog_cache_lean.py`: clean.

## 2026-08-06/07 — `watch_list.mode`+`dry_run` collapsed into a single `state` column (2 paired Opus reviews + an exhaustive sweep, ~30 bugs fixed); real GDXU incident found, root-caused, and fixed (2 more silent-failure bugs closed, position reconciled for real, a ground-truth sweep tool built); that fix set itself paired-reviewed, found unreachable/incomplete, and re-fixed

Two distinct major threads, both real-money-adjacent, both went through the mandatory paired-review process.

**Thread 1 — the state collapse.** Started as a narrowly-scoped per-node `dry_run` override, then the user pushed for the full collapse mid-session ("It's really gonna bug me if we don't simplify it. Full literal column replacement."): `watch_list.mode` ('research'/'live') and account-level `dry_run` are now one `state` column (`'paper'`/`'dry_run'`/`'live'`, mutually exclusive/exhaustive). `schwab_safety.AccountLimits.dry_run` renamed `trading_enabled` (inverted semantics). Real gate: `real_order_allowed = (node.state=='live') AND (account.trading_enabled==True)`, account ceiling independently checked, never absorbed into node.state. Position-lifecycle state (trigger-buy/arming/trailing-sell as a shared enum) was raised and explicitly deferred — the next genuinely new strategy paradigm should own its own state tracking internally, not a shared generic layer.

Two full paired Opus reviews (independent-cold + contextual, rebuttal exchange) + one exhaustive third-agent sweep, ~50 production files + ~30 scripts touched, ~30 real findings fixed. Most serious: a Slack button metadata whitelist omitted `state` (fail-open real-order risk on a "Filled" tap); ~13 `node_dry_run` call sites failed open on any unexpected state value (now fail closed, `!= 'live'`); and a **CRITICAL, reproduced against a real DB copy**: a legacy column-ladder line in `ensure_tables()` unconditionally resurrected the dropped `mode` column (defaulted `'live'` on every row) on the very next daemon restart after migration — fixed, re-verified 3x against a real DB copy. On reflection with the user, downgraded to MEDIUM once confirmed nothing in the codebase still reads `mode` — the real risk was operator confusion + a latent future rebuild-migration crash, not an active trading bug. `add_node`'s default (`state='live'`, unvalidated) survived a full 46-call-site audit before flipping to `'paper'` + adding validation; 8 more real crash sites (a `mode=MODE` variable-based kwarg, missed by both Opus reviews' literal-string greps) found via a separate AST-based sweep.

Migration applied to the real `cache/live/trading_live.db` after backing it up and killing the daemon; 21 read-only scripts diffed before/after against the real DB, all clean. Daemon restarted clean. Full suite 611/611.

**Thread 2 — the GDXU incident.** Spot-checking `soxl_ira` post-migration surfaced a real, unprotected broker position (2 shares GDXU, +35% unrealized) with zero local record at all. Root-caused via `coverage_events` + a prior session's own transcript (not guessed): a Claude Sonnet 5 assistant in an earlier session used `stage_live_test_order.py` (the deliberate direct-broker-bypass tool for staging real order tests) to place a real, deliberately undersized trailing-buy meant to organically prove `post_fill_topup` — the tool's own node-lookup failed, silently skipped creating a `pending_buys` row, and the real fill sat invisible for a week. A second, independent bug compounded it: `_reconcile_buy_fill`'s `if not pendings: return` was completely silent, conflating "already reconciled" with "never tracked at all." Confirmed via call-chain tracing: the `post_fill_topup` proof this test existed to produce never happened either — the whole downstream chain never had an entry point.

Position reconciled for real: node flipped to `state='live'` (required for a non-simulated stop), `open_position()` called with the real backdated entry, then the real arm-detection path fired and placed a genuine `TRAILING_STOP SELL` at the broker — confirmed directly against Schwab's order book. Rehearsed via a new fake_broker test *before* touching the real broker. Also built: an on-demand (explicitly not periodic, per the user's correction — "when I ask you for state, I expect state") ground-truth sweep, `scripts/check_untracked_positions.py` + `schwab_client.get_all_real_positions`, directly instantiating `automation_principles.md` #1. Separately found: `seed_baseline_config.py`'s drift-check `FIELDS` never tracked the 10 overlay columns — fixed + backfilled into all 24 existing rows, re-verified zero drift.

**Thread 2b — the fix set's own paired review.** Per CLAUDE.md's mandatory convention, this incremental diff got its own paired review (independent-cold + contextual + rebuttal exchange) before commit. Both reviews independently converged on the same core finding: **the new orphan-fill alert was itself unreachable for the exact scenario it was built for** — every caller of `_reconcile_buy_fill` except `drain_fill_queue` iterates `pending_buys` (can never observe a fully orphaned fill), and `drain_fill_queue` itself short-circuited at the auto-fill-detection opt-in gate before ever calling it. 18 findings total, all fixed:
- `drain_fill_queue` gained a dedicated orphan-fill branch (confirms via a real broker poll, alerts, doesn't attempt to reconcile — no node to attribute it to).
- `_reconcile_buy_fill`'s "already reconciled" check replaced with a new `db.get_real_open_position(ticker, account)` — the old ticker-only/all-accounts/dry-run-sim-inclusive check could be fooled by a same-ticker synthetic canary position in a different account.
- `stage_live_test_order.py`: `--wl-id` now validated against `--ticker`/`--account` (unvalidated, it could misdirect a real order's tracking to the wrong ticker and later drive a real MARKET BUY against it); fail-closed check now requires `state=='live'` (a resolved `dry_run` node would place a real order the daemon's own fill synthesis then re-orphans a second way); check widened from `TRAILING`+`BUY` only to any real BUY (`MARKET` had zero coverage — the still-open `market_buy_placement` go-live item, same exposure, faster fill).
- The failure event moved off the `buy_fill_reconciled` scenario_key (no `bad_results` declared) to a distinct `orphaned_fill_detected` key — was rendering as false verified-live proof of the mechanism it proves failed.
- `check_untracked_positions.py` rewritten: distinguishes algo-relevant tickers from hand-held non-algo holdings (was permanently red on every real account); widened account scope; fetch errors now count as findings; accounts for open `addon_legs`; catches NULL-account rows; sums duplicate ticker rows.
- `get_all_real_positions` sums rather than overwrites duplicates; new `get_all_real_short_positions` (a naked short was previously invisible — the most dangerous state the sweep could miss).
- `seed_baseline_config.py` gained `--merge-new-fields` (safe, idempotent — never overwrites an already-tracked value) so a future `FIELDS` addition is self-applying instead of needing another ad-hoc backfill.
- 2 new fake_broker tests (`test_fake_broker_orphaned_fill_alert_scenario.py`) proving the orphan-fill alert fires for a genuinely untracked fill and stays silent for a normal one.

**Verification**: full suite 614/614 (611 baseline + 3 new tests this round), `live_sim_harness.py` 7/7 (run twice, before and after the fix-set review), `signals_invariants.py` clean throughout both threads.

Whether `stage_live_test_order.py`'s fail-closed pattern should be audited into `scripts/live_sanity_check.py` or other bypass tools — flagged, not done.

Picked up the open 2026-08-07 (late) backlog finding ("18-ticker watchlist is NOT liquidity-limited") and built the actual screening + backfill pipeline for it.

**Screening**: `scripts/liquidity_screen_candidates.py` ranks untested leveraged tickers by 1% ADV notional, excluding single-stock underliers and already-swept tickers. **Backfill pipeline**: `scripts/run_liquidity_tranches.sh` — 13 idempotent tranches (`--status`/`--reset` flags, marker-file-based resume). Tranche 1 is deliberately just SQQQ alone as a validation round, since a real gap was found in `prune_backtest_cache.py`: it doesn't group by `entry_timing`, confirmed live-triggerable on AGQ/GDXD's historical data (9 groups affected) — not fixed this session (out of scope, and the current campaign only sweeps `open_check` so it doesn't affect new tranches), just logged. Per-tranche sequence: sweep → locate best node (pre-prune) → prune (dry-run/build/swap) → locate best node (post-prune) → **hard stop, no marker, if the winning row changed** → overlay shim → marker. Confirmed the sweep engine's parallelism is per-ticker (saturates all workers on one ticker's own grid), not cross-ticker — no efficiency loss from small tranches, only added prune-pass overhead (each pass rescans the whole table, measured >60s already, confirmed non-trivial).

**New infra for the overlay smoke-test**: `scripts/locate_best_node.py` (best-row locator, reusing `load_nodes()`'s exact column mapping rather than reinterpreting `backtest_cache`'s known-overloaded columns fresh; `candidate_nodes` interim registry table, deduped by full param tuple, standing in for a real `wl_id` since no promotion has happened yet — added after the user asked "what if we ran another node?" exposed that overlay rows weren't traceable back to their source config). `scripts/run_overlay_shim.py` runs both drought overlay (`drought_overlay_test.py`'s real functions) and margin add-on (`stacked_model/add_on.py::generate_addon_trades`) against a constructed candidate node with zero watch_list footprint, writing to `candidate_overlay_results` (joined against `candidate_nodes`). `scripts/candidate_node_sensitivity.py` — full-axis (not just one param) sensitivity sweep, built per `docs/cliff_safety_query_checklist.md`'s explicit fixed-vs-varied convention.

**Real findings** (`docs/research_log.md`'s two 2026-08-07 entries): SQQQ's core sweep is fragile/cliff on both strategies (TB worst_neighbor -92.3%, TE outright negative alpha) — not a clean candidate on the one ticker fully validated. Drought/add-on overlay results are sensitive to node params, but **not uniformly** — refined via the full-axis sweep: axes that redefine entry-signal timing (`window`, `z_score_threshold`, `trail_buy_pct`'s fill mechanic) are fragile (jaccard 0.27-0.32); axes that only shape exit/risk behavior (`max_hold_hours`, `trail_sell_pct`, `arm_sell_pct`) are robust (jaccard 0.53-1.00). ## 2026-08-08 — [Research] Candidate report built out: fill-resolution accuracy, annualized excess, real per-node overlay, liquidity, and a self-consistency bug found in cliff-safety itself

Started from broadening the prior session's fill-resolution-accuracy check (25→66 signals, 6→17 tickers), confirming "possible" is still the most accurate single resolution but that it doesn't generalize into a selection-metric change: a 3-way candidate comparison (`scripts/candidate_5min_report.py`, new) across 19 liquidity-screen tickers showed selecting by raw "possible" alone picks a strictly worse-robustness node in 7/19 cases for little accuracy gain — confirms keeping `robust_alpha = MIN(...)` as the real selection criterion.

**Built `scripts/candidate_summary_report.py` into the canonical, growing candidate report** (user's explicit call: "we just need to keep adding to it"), through several rounds of user-driven redesign:
- Real liquidity column (`avg_vol_10d*last_price*0.01`) — a "liquidity-screen" report had none.
- CAGR-based `ann_excess_pct` (`scripts/annualized_alpha_report.py`, new) fixing a real cross-ticker comparability bug: raw `alpha_vs_spy` spans wildly different real calendar windows per ticker (SOXL/AGQ/DPST ~3.0y cached history vs SPCL ~0.31y) since `compute_bh_returns` computes `spy_bh` over each ticker's own full data range. Annualizing re-ranks candidates significantly (JNUG: raw-alpha rank 4 → annualized-excess #1).
- Restructured to **3 rows per ticker** (best safe node / best unsafe node / 5min best possible), not 1 — user's call, to sanity-check the "safe" pick isn't missing something and to compare SPY-adjusted vs raw returns directly.
- All 3 rows now get **real, independently-computed** drought/addon overlay (new `run_overlay_shim.run_for_node()`, runs the shim against an arbitrary node instead of only the ticker's auto-picked best) — not a shared ticker-level number, per the user's explicit call that all three should get equal treatment.
- CSV/xlsx export (xlsx: Candidates + Column Definitions glossary sheet, one `COLUMN_DEFS` source of truth shared with the Streamlit page) — delivered twice to the user as the design evolved.
- New `pages/15_Candidates.py` (Streamlit): sortable/reorderable/downloadable via `st.dataframe`'s native toolbar, reuses the CLI script's functions directly.

**Real bug found and fixed, with a full investigation**: the restructure exposed a self-inconsistency — a node labeled "best safe node" showed Status=CLIFF in the same report. Root cause: this report's `worst_neighbor()` checked `max_hold_hours` neighbors at `±24h` (copied from `prune_backtest_cache.py`'s keep-threshold convention) while `top_safe_nodes.best_safe_node()` (which actually produces the "safe" label) checks `±7h` — a units/radius mismatch, not a real disagreement about safety. Investigated whether the wider `±24h` should become the new standard instead: confirmed `max_hold_hours` is swept at a **uniform 7-hour step in 100% of 11,613 real campaigns** (zero exceptions), so this reduces cleanly to "radius=1 step vs radius=3 steps" (matching `CLIFF_RADIUS=3` already used for take_profit/stop_loss) rather than a density/units problem. **User's explicit call: keep radius=1** (didn't want a 3-trading-day-wide hold tolerance as the real standard) — fixed this report's `worst_neighbor()` to `±7h`, decision logged in `docs/cliff_safety_query_checklist.md` so it isn't re-litigated. `prune_backtest_cache.py`'s own `±24` keep-threshold left untouched — user's call, kept as a wider retention safety margin for a possible future bespoke island analysis, not something to change as a side effect of this report.

**Overlay robustness stress test** (`candidate_overlay_robustness_check.py`) run against the batch's positive addon/drought results (15 checks, ticker/mechanism/node-id disambiguated across several re-registered `candidate_nodes` rows): KOLD addon, TNA drought (all 3 variants), UGL addon (one variant), and URTY drought (both variants) flip negative with their biggest winner removed — fragile, not a repeatable signal. **New `scripts/candidate_full_review.py`** (one row per ticker × candidate-selection-type, no hard filters — only indicative `_tranche` columns): 4 candidate types (added `best certain`, closing a real asymmetry — `pessimistic`/`certain` previously only ever floored `robust_alpha`, never got their own ranking axis; surfaced a genuinely different, much safer SOXL node worst_neighbor +197.6% vs the standard pick's +5.6%); raw CAGR + all three fill-resolution alphas as separate columns; sector + K-1/UBTI status (only for tickers actually confirmed via a real source check, everything else honestly "not checked"); overlay robustness (chronological split + single-trade-removal); a real 5-fold walk-forward reusing `walk_forward_check.py` against each row's exact node (not just the old v4/TrailingBoth-only path); max/current drawdown (free — reuses walk-forward's own trade list); same-day-block sensitivity/stability (TrailingBoth-only, a 2nd real kernel run); 30d/90d macro trend; a real yfinance stock-split check; and trailing-sell 5-min resolution accuracy (the exit-side mirror of the existing entry-side check).

**Paired review (Fable independent-cold + Opus contextual, both converged independently) found 2 HIGH + several MEDIUM real bugs, all fixed and verified**: the walk-forward input cache was keyed `(ticker, strategy)` without `window`, silently reusing one candidate's indicators for another's walk-forward/drawdown/same-day-block checks whenever a ticker had rows at different windows (15+ tickers affected) — fixed, verified against Opus's own independently-computed before/after numbers on GDXD (exact match). The stability (70/30) split compared the blocked/unblocked variants at two different calendar dates and used a full-window SPY benchmark for half-period comparisons — fixed to match `train_test_split_check.py`'s established per-half-benchmark/shared-cut-time convention. `alpha_retention_pct`'s sign inverted when the unblocked baseline was negative, mislabeling a `HIGH_RETENTION` case that was actually worse — fixed with a sign guard, raw before/after values always exposed regardless. Checklist item 3 (trailing-sell resolution) was scoped but never implemented — added. Also fixed, found only by running the real 82-ticker batch (not by the paired review): `verify_fill_resolution_accuracy.py` used `None` instead of `np.nan` for a missing resolution key, crashing `.abs()` on an object-dtype column whenever a resolution was missing for every real signal — first caller to run at enough scale to hit it.

**Certain-resolution kernel bug, found, fixed, and paired-reviewed.** `backtester.py`'s `_simulate_trail_both` certain branch had two real bugs: a missing frozen-trigger case (a bar whose own Low doesn't move `running_low` has its trigger fixed for the whole bar — a High-touch is exactly as certain as an Open-gap, but the old code only ever checked Close-confirmation and needlessly deferred these — 40% of SOXL's own fills were this case) and an unproven Close-crediting formula. Fixed both, added a lean `_simulate_certain_only`/`run_backtest_certain_only` for future cheaper recomputes. A required paired independent+contextual Opus review (kernel file changed) found a CONFIRMED HIGH issue in the first-pass Close-crediting fix (credited the bar's raw Close — provably always ≥ the old buggy credit, but not actually a proven no-guess price); a direct isolation test confirmed this, not the frozen-trigger fix, was the dominant driver of the reported 2x-11x per-ticker drop. Refixed to credit `min(buy_trigger_prior, high)`, the genuinely tight worst-case-price bound both reviewers verified mathematically; updated the two stale Python mirrors that had drifted from the kernel (`export_trades.py`, `verify_fill_resolution_accuracy.py` — the latter being the tool whose "possible is 94% accurate" finding justifies the possible-as-default decision); added 4 pinned regression tests (`tests/test_certain_resolution_fix.py`) closing the "unenforced instruction" gap the reviewers flagged. **Corrected a wrong claim made earlier in the same session**: "KORU flips to a real loss" was from a since-discarded hand-mirror missing the frozen-trigger fix — the real kernel-verified value is positive, fixed in `research_log.md`/`deep_backlog.md`/`backlog_cache.md`. **User's explicit call: table the full `backtest_cache` certain-column recompute (~5M rows) and the broader possible-only-tooling architectural gap — `possible` stays the working default** (also the empirically stronger/more-frequently-winning resolution). Full backtester-scoped suite (82 tests) + the 4 new tests pass, no regressions.

**Real K1/underlier-count screener built.** New `tickers` columns (`k1_status`/`underlier_count`/`underlier_note`), migrated `candidate_full_review.py` off its hardcoded `K1_STATUS` dict, hand-researched 22 tickers directly then delegated the remaining 69 to a background research agent (returned as JSON, written to the DB from the main session after the agent's git-worktree isolation turned out to lack the gitignored DB — caught before any writes were lost). New findings: GLL/KOLD/UGL/UVXY confirmed K-1 (same ProShares family as AGQ/USO/BOIL); BULZ disqualified (15 holdings, below the 20-security minimum, joining FNGU/QPUX/SPCL); a new user-set rule — single-commodity/single-bond-future tickers (GLL/KOLD/UGL/TBT/TMF/TMV) are out of scope by default, broad-index trading is the core premise, AGQ is the one deliberate exception for its Section 1256 60/40 tax treatment — applied via pick='no' on all 16 matching nodes. Crypto-linked single-underlier tickers (ETHU/SOLT/BITU/BITX/BTCZ) are explicitly NOT disqualified — separate, explicit ruling that crypto itself is in scope.

**`candidate_full_review.py` gained 3 CAGR-stacking columns** (`core_addon_cagr_pct`/`core_drought_cagr_pct`/`core_both_cagr_pct`), each overlay gated on its own robustness verdict (a FRAGILE overlay contributes a no-op 1x factor, not its raw number) — multiplicative, not additive (two ~1.5x-robust overlays combine to ~2.3x, not ~4x). Also wired the drought vol-gate's `REAL_SELECTION` verdict (previously purely diagnostic, never fed back into any reported number) to actually override the plain drought factor when confirmed. `--csv`/`--xlsx` outputs are now always timestamped (were silently overwriting on every run before).

**Process notes for next time**: caught and corrected several real mid-session mistakes — misreading the liquidity column's units (already 1% of ADV, not raw), quoting the wrong CSV column as "CAGR," a job-tmp-vs-output/ directory mixup, CSV-vs-xlsx format mismatch, and (most consequential) trusting a hand-written Python mirror script without verifying it against the real kernel, which is what let the wrong KORU claim through in the first place. New memories saved for all of these; `possible`'s existing `simulate_trail_both_annotated` mirror WAS separately verified this session and found exact, which is the discipline that should apply to any future hand-rolled mirror.

**All 5 follow-ups from the RETL/LABD-shaped add-on buying-power fix (`docs/deep_backlog.md`'s 2026-08-09/10 entry) closed.** Items 2-5 fixed directly: stale "kept strict" comment in `schwab_safety.check_order` corrected, `scripts/coverage_registry.py` gained rows for `addon_buying_power_check`/`addon_second_ticker_buy_allowed`, the failing test rewritten as 3 real cases (allowed-when-sufficient, blocked-when-insufficient, blocked-unpriced). Item 1 (the `ADDON_BUYING_POWER_HEADROOM_MULT` 2x-vs-1x reservation asymmetry) was deliberately NOT fixed as a math change — user's explicit direction: add a daily daemon job (`signals_notify.check_addon_buying_power_drift`) monitoring whether `buying_power == cash` still holds for every account hosting a live `addon_enabled` node, alerting unconditionally on divergence rather than scaling the reservation.

**Same session, two more asks against the pre-existing `check_live_state_reconciliation`** (broker-vs-local-DB state check, unrelated to the add-on fix): (a) retry a broker-fetch failure up to 3 total attempts, 3s apart, alerting once exhausted instead of silently skipping; (b) moved the check earlier in `active_signals.py`'s poll loop, right after `check_sl_order_fills`'s `open_positions` refresh, so it runs before SELL/BUY actions are considered that cycle.

**3-way paired review** (Opus independent-cold + Fable independent-cold + Opus contextual, all launched in parallel — user specifically asked for Fable on the independent-cold slot, per the established Fable+Opus pairing pattern from prior sessions) converged strongly, catching real bugs before any of it shipped:
- **[HIGH, all 3]** New reconciliation fetch-failure alert had no cooldown, unlike every sibling alert in the file — a sustained broker outage would flood Slack every ~5min per position (up to 11 messages/cycle on `soxl_ira`). Fixed: per-account cooldown (`_RECONCILE_FETCH_FAIL_ALERTED`) + the post wrapped in try/except (a separate catch from Opus independent-cold: an unguarded post failure would abort reconciliation for every remaining position that cycle).
- **[HIGH, all 3]** The retry sleeps now sat ahead of the time-critical pinned entry/exit scans. Fixed: once an account exhausts retries once per poll cycle, later positions on that same account skip straight to the failure path with no further sleep — bounds added latency to O(#accounts down), not O(#positions).
- **[MED/HIGH, all 3]** `check_addon_buying_power_drift`'s original global once-per-day watermark advanced even on total fetch failure (contextual review: `get_account_buying_power`'s own docstring flags the `buyingPower` field as unverified, so a `KeyError` there could silently kill the monitor permanently, every day). Fixed: rebuilt around a per-account `checked` map — an account only marks done after a successful compare, and a diverged account whose Slack post doesn't confirm stays unmarked too (mirrors `check_intraday_risk_review`'s existing confirmed-post pattern).
- **[LOW, multiple]** `result="failed_closed"` mislabel renamed to `fetch_failed`; hardcoded `mode="live"` replaced with `_coverage_mode(account)`; a false "same workaround as check_intraday_risk_review's siblings" comment corrected; `coverage_registry.py`'s new row had a factually wrong "real live events on file" claim (verified against the live DB: zero exist) — corrected; a dead `blocked_addon_leg` result string still cited in an unrelated comment — corrected to `blocked_insufficient`; `schwab_safety.check_order`'s top docstring only got half of item 2's original fix (still said "cash permitting" for the add-on path, now buying-power-based) — corrected.

All 3 reviewers independently confirmed the retry-counting math, drift-comparison sign, `ADDON_BUYING_POWER_HEADROOM_MULT`-not-touched claim, and the poll-loop move's lack of stale-data risk were all correct as originally written.

**Verification**: full suite 705 passed (was 701 pre-session), `signals_invariants.py` clean, `verify_trailing_buy_resolution.py`/`verify_trailing_sell_resolution.py --tickers AGQ,SOXL` both clean (no new mismatch), `scripts/live_sim_harness.py` 7/7. ## 2026-08-10 (later) — Closed the one `not-instrumented` coverage-registry gap (`drought_handoff_alert_slot_preserved`); paired Opus + this-session Fable review found and fixed a real false-verified-live risk

**Instrumentation added**: `active_signals._scan_buy_signals`'s `already_held` branch (the fix from `docs/plans/real_order_execution_drought_addon.md` 0.6/5.4 that releases the once-per-day `buy_alerted` slot while a real drought HANDOFF is still in flight) now calls `db.log_coverage_event`. This was the only genuinely `not-instrumented` row left in `scripts/coverage_registry.py`'s 67-row Grid (surfaced while validating overall test coverage per the user's ask). The existing test for this scenario was rewritten to actually drive the real `active_signals._scan_buy_signals` (previously it only hand-replicated the branch logic without asserting anything real) — caught in the process that the old test's key shape (`(node['id'], 'z')`) never matched what production code actually uses (bare `node['id']`).

**Paired review** (Opus independent-cold + Opus contextual + a this-session-only Fable architecture/test-coverage sweep, run in parallel per the user's explicit one-off request — not a standing CLAUDE.md change) converged strongly on one real finding: the release condition is `_handoff_in_flight OR db.get_drought_pending_buy(...)` — a still-resting drought *entry* order (pre-handoff, not the unwind race this row exists to prove) also releases the slot, and the original instrumentation logged both sub-cases under one identical `result="slot_released"`. Since `compute_status` buckets purely on `(mode, result)` with `bad_results=[]` for this row, a single live firing from the pending-entry sub-case alone could flip the Grid row to `verified-live` without the actual HANDOFF race ever having fired — exactly the false-green the registry exists to prevent. **Fixed**: split into two distinct `result` values (`slot_released_handoff` vs `slot_released_pending_entry`), corrected the registry row's notes to state this explicitly, and fixed a smaller LOW (`_coverage_mode` called without the in-scope `node` arg — could mislabel `mode='live'` for a non-live node).

Fable also flagged (MEDIUM) no negative-control test existed proving the slot **stays burned** absent a handoff/pending cause — added, plus a dedicated test for the previously-untested `get_drought_pending_buy`-only arm. 9/9 tests pass in the file; the scoped slice (`pytest -k "drought or scan_buy_signals or coverage_registry"`, 34 tests) passes clean. Full 705-test suite was run twice unnecessarily during this wrap for a change this narrowly scoped — user pushback ("we need to be a little better about slightly more focused testing," "~75% of the code was nowhere near impact"), recorded in the `feedback_scope_test_runs_to_the_change` memory as a recurrence.

**Checklist verification**: `signals_invariants.py` — 1 pre-existing, unrelated violation found (DPST `wl_id=197` config drift from baseline, from the other concurrently-running live-trading session's promotion-shortlist work, not this session's change — left untouched). `verify_trailing_buy_resolution.py --tickers AGQ,SOXL` and `verify_trailing_sell_resolution.py --tickers AGQ,SOXL` both clean, no mismatches. `scripts/live_sim_harness.py` 7/7.

## 2026-08-10 (later still) — `node_id` threaded through schwab_client's order-placement chain (AGQ/brokerage collision fix); pytest-xdist made the default (~3.2x faster); paired review found+fixed 1 HIGH + 2 MEDIUM before shipping

**Root question ("why so many tickers on brokerage") led to a real bug**: `watch_list` has three nodes sharing `ticker='AGQ', account='brokerage'` (ids 41/193 `dry_run`, 203 `live`, $231). `schwab_safety.check_order`'s own code comment already flagged this ambiguity as a KNOWN LIMITATION since the 2026-07-25/26 wl_id refactor — a ticker+account-derived node lookup returns `None` on collision, silently making a node-level automation pause a no-op and letting the BUY/SELL position guards resolve to whichever sibling's position has the latest `entry_time`. Harmless today only because `brokerage.trading_enabled=False`.

**Real fix, per the user's explicit direction** (not a relocation, unlike JNUG's same-day fix): added `node_id: int | None = None` to all 8 of `schwab_client.py`'s order-placement/replace functions, threaded through `schwab_safety.approve_and_record` into `check_order`. All 16 real production call sites in `signals_notify.py` updated to pass it. Backward-compatible (`None` default preserves old ambiguous-derivation behavior for any caller not yet updated — none remain in production).

**Concurrent-session collision handled mid-session**: another session was independently editing the same working tree (no worktree isolation) — `signals_db.py`/`signals_helpers.py`/`scripts/coverage_check.py` for an unrelated `get_full_position_state` feature, overlapping in `schwab_client.py`. Coordinated via a direct message exchange before either committed; confirmed no file-level overlap, combined diff green (728/728 from their side), committed together in `a319c9f`.

**Session-wrap paired review (independent-cold + contextual Opus, run in parallel) found real gaps in the fix as first shipped — all confirmed and fixed same session**:
- **[HIGH]** BUY existing-position guard could fail OPEN: `get_open_position_by_wl_id(node_id)` alone misses a legacy/unbackfilled `wl_id IS NULL` position (a real, documented case in `signals_db.open_position()`, though zero such rows exist in the live DB today) — would let a second real BUY through against real, untracked capital. SELL mirror was failing CLOSED (blocking a genuine exit) for the same reason. **Fixed**: new `signals_db.get_orphaned_open_position_for_account` (strictly `wl_id IS NULL`-scoped, never falls back to a sibling's real position) checked whenever the primary wl_id lookup misses, on both sides.
- **[MEDIUM]** `node_id` was trusted unverified — a caller passing a stale/wrong node's id would silently apply its automation-pause/position state to the wrong order. **Fixed**: `check_order` now verifies the node's `(ticker, account)` matches, falling back to the old ambiguous derivation (not raising) on mismatch, with a new `node_id_ticker_account_mismatch` coverage event.
- **[MEDIUM]** `record_node_streak` (the node circuit breaker) was still called from all 24 of `schwab_client.py`'s call sites via the old ambiguous derivation, even though `node_id` was already a local at each site — would have silently defeated the circuit breaker for AGQ/`brokerage` once live. **Fixed**: all 24 sites now pass `node_id`.
- **[MEDIUM, confirmed real, deliberately deferred]**: duplicate-order guards and `check_live_state_reconciliation` still assume `(ticker, account)` uniqueness — can't be fixed by `node_id` threading alone (Schwab's own APIs have no node concept). Not reachable today (AGQ's only `live` node is 203). New backlog item: don't promote a 2nd `live` sibling on any `(ticker, account)` pair before addressing this.
- **[LOW]** Both original regression tests only covered the automation-pause path, not the higher-consequence position guards. Added 2 more tests (fake-venue sibling-collision + the orphaned-row fallback directly) — 4 new tests total, all passing.

**`pytest-xdist` made the default** (`pytest.ini`, `addopts = -n auto`) after confirming no test touches the real `trading_live.db` without isolation and the live daemon wasn't running — cut the full suite from ~15.5min to ~5min (~3.2x). Surfaced 2 pre-existing flaky tests in the process (`test_entry_abandon.py`/`test_overlay_paper_trading.py`, both real-`datetime.now()`-dependent, confirmed unrelated to this session's code — pass reliably standalone), logged as one open backlog item.

Fixed via `--dist=loadscope`: 45/45 passing across 3 repeated runs (was 6-12 failures/run), 757/757 full suite, no timing regression.

**Per-ticker `force_same_day_block` override, built after a multi-round clarification** (user initially said "block margin accounts too," then corrected to "override the ticker... not to be blocked," then corrected again: "not supposed to be at the account level — should be per ticker"): new `watch_list.force_same_day_block` column (nullable→default-0, migrated into all 3 `ensure_tables()` schema paths including both `watch_list_new` rebuild blocks), `signals_db.set_force_same_day_block(wl_id, enabled)` setter (audit-logged), and `schwab_safety.check_order`'s existing `same_day_block` guard (previously margin-exempt only) now also blocks when the resolved node's own flag is set — re-fetched fresh, not reused from earlier in the function. Default off everywhere; user's explicit call was to build it and decide who gets it later, not enable it now.

**Required session-wrap paired review (independent-cold + contextual Opus, run_optimization_sweep.py + signals_db.py + schwab_safety.py diffs) found a CRITICAL real-money gap before it could bite**: the entire `same_day_block` section (including the new override) ran unconditionally ahead of `check_order`'s `is_protective`/`is_addon_leg` exemptions, which only ever covered a different guard (duplicate-open-position) further down. Since both live-enabled accounts (`ira`, `soxl_ira`) are margin, `force_same_day_block` was the ONLY way `same_day_block` could ever fire on real capital — meaning once enabled on any node, a sanctioned post-fill top-up (`is_protective=True`, e.g. `post_fill_topup`, real-live-proven 2026-08-10 on RETL) landing on a same-day-exit day would have been wrongly rejected. This gap was pre-existing for cash accounts but never reachable (no cash account has ever been `trading_enabled`) — the new feature was about to make it reachable for the first time. ## 2026-08-11 — Deep wash-sale review led to a real universe-wide data-backfill bug (Opus-confirmed root cause); JNUG moved ira→brokerage, SOXS+LABU promoted (with real course-correction), `v5.1` sweep version + 33-ticker resweep queued

**Wash-sale deep dive** (JNUG): walked through wash-sale mechanics end to end using `scripts/sim_wash_sale_impact.py`, extended with JNUG's real node config, a `--overlay` flag for drought re-entries, and fixed the notional model to compound trade-to-trade instead of resetting each trade (was giving wrong basis math). Confirmed JNUG's real cadence produces near-total wash-sale gridlock (same shape as SOXL) but zero permanent loss at this trade frequency — every deferred-loss chain resolves within weeks. Real accidental cross-account wash sale (GDXU, incident #2, already on file) discussed at length — confirmed Schwab's 1099-B can't see cross-account wash sales at all (same-account only), so that one needs manual CPA reporting every year, permanently, since the source document never self-corrects.
