ETHU/AGQ `brokerage` nodes got `addon_enabled=1`. SOXS promoted to `ira` ($10k, candidate id=182, CAGR-first pick) with a daily-track paper twin. LABU promoted to `brokerage`, downgraded to `paper` per explicit request (not going live yet).

**Root-cause investigation, the big one**: routine BTCZ/WEBL K-1 research pulled a thread — confirmed GDXU/NUGT (and eventually 215 tickers) were silently under-backfilled: ~13 months of cached hourly history when yfinance actually has ~35 months available for free (a fetch-window bug, not the documented "would need a paid vendor" limitation). Root-caused to `data_collector.py`'s fragile `period="1y"` fallback mock (only fires if importing the real `data_manager.fetch_live_data_smart` fails) plus evidence of a stray non-cron continuous-loop invocation from 2026-06-26 that never restarted — mechanism not fully pinned down, logged as trading_incidents id=4. Built `scripts/backfill_hourly_history.py` (safe prepend-merge, existing rows always win on overlap) and ran it across all 213+5 affected tickers — 190 successfully extended, 23 genuinely delisted/no-data.

**The reproducibility bug that mattered more**: cross-checking same-day-block CAGR sensitivity for LABU showed 71 trades in an archived report vs 75 in a fresh recompute of the identical node. Spawned an Opus agent (isolated worktree) to root-cause independently rather than keep guessing at 3am — found it wasn't a kernel bug at all: `strategy_cagr_pct = cagr(cached_abs_return_pct, freshly_recomputed_years)` silently mixes a stale cached return with a freshly-recomputed years denominator once the underlying data grows — real example, SOXS showed 93.4% CAGR in one run and 28.6% in a later run, same node, same stale return, only `years` changed. `dispatch_parallel_grid`'s cache-hit check has zero data-freshness awareness, so a naive resweep would silently skip every already-covered grid point.

**Fix**: version-bump to `v5.1` for tickers whose raw data actually changed. Of 216 changed tickers, 40 already had `v5` coverage (need real resweep to escape the skip trap); of the 56 real liquidity-tranche tickers specifically, 33 need a genuine resweep, 23 didn't (their `v5` rows copied forward to `v5.1` directly, ~1.62M rows, no wasted compute). New `backtest_cache.copied_from_version` column distinguishes genuine recomputes from carried-forward copies. `run_liquidity_tranches.sh` updated (both the sweep call and a second, easy-to-miss `run_overlay_shim.py --version` default that would've silently stayed on stale nodes even after the sweep moved to v5.1) and launched by the user at session end.

**SOXS course-correction, worth remembering**: originally promoted on a self-consistent 93.4% CAGR (valid for the 1.11-year window that existed at decision time) — reverted to `paper` when the mixing bug was found, then restored to `live` once the user correctly pointed out the original number wasn't wrong, just now-knowably-incomplete given more real history exists. Real full-window recompute: 40.0% CAGR, genuinely lower but trustworthy, vs. the corrupted 28.6% a naive rerun would show.

**Explicitly declined**: filtering the v5.1 resweep list by liquidity/K-1/single-underlier ("if I pick a node that compliance doesn't like I'll deal with it") — confirmed UGL's exclusion (single-commodity, out of scope by the existing rule with AGQ as the sole named exception) stays as originally decided, not re-litigated.

**Also found**: the other concurrent session built a real per-node `watch_list.force_same_day_block` override (uncommitted) — independent of `account_type`, motivated by this exact same-day-block CAGR work. LABU is the one node (of ~14 checked) where the block genuinely helps (76.6% vs 73.0%, modest ~3.6pp), not yet flagged on its node.

Two `trading_incidents` logged (id=4 data gap/stale process, id=5 the reproducibility bug — later resolved by Opus, not a real bug in the kernel). `docs/backlog_cache.md` gained two open items: the LABU/TNA/SOXS candidate note (removed per user correction — wasn't wanted there) and the `candidate_full_review.py` cross-version search gap (real, not started). `docs/design.md` gained a full write-up of the v5.1 mechanism. No `active_signals.py`/`signals_*.py`/`schwab_*.py`/backtest-kernel files touched this session (only DB data, `scripts/sim_wash_sale_impact.py`, and the new `scripts/backfill_hourly_history.py`) — paired-review gate not triggered by the letter of the rule, though the Opus investigation agent effectively served that role for the one real finding that mattered.

## 2026-08-11 (late) — Hardcoded account config replaced with a DB-backed `accounts` table ("Option 1.5"); real live DB migrated; paired Opus review found+fixed 1 HIGH + 3 MEDIUM + 2 LOW

Two new real Schwab accounts (`brokerage` $20k genuine Reg-T margin, `roth` $60k confirmed real limited-margin) were funded and linked this session, exposing a real architectural problem: `schwab_safety.ACCOUNTS` (hardcoded dict) and `schwab_client.NICKNAMES` (a separate hardcoded list) were kept in sync only by convention, and two known bugs made a manual rename/add unsafe — a substring-based tax-advantaged-account guess (3 places) that admitted it would fail open on a future account name like "hsa", and an overloaded `account_type` field conflating same-day cash-settlement eligibility with real margin-borrowing capability (already known wrong for `soxl_ira`).

**Design, validated by an independent Opus consultation and explicit user sign-off ("Option 1.5")**: keep the 5 existing alias strings as the real primary key (no surrogate-ID migration, no rename, zero data migration on the 11 tables — confirmed via live `PRAGMA table_info` sweep, not the originally-assumed 7 — that already store `account` as free text). New `accounts` table replaces both hardcoded structures; `account_type` splits into `cash_settlement_type` + new `margin_capable`; a new `is_tax_advantaged` column (NOT NULL, no default) replaces all 3 substring guards, failing loud on an unknown account instead of guessing; new `retired_at` column (an alias is retired, never renamed/reused); new `signals_invariants.check_all_account_values_are_known_aliases` replaces the FK enforcement the plain-TEXT columns lack, split into live-state tables (non-retired aliases only) vs. historical/log tables (any alias ever, so retiring one doesn't make the check permanently red).

**Critical scope decision with explicit user sign-off**: today's real add-on-margin gate already passes for `ira`/`soxl_ira` (8 real live `soxl_ira` `addon_enabled` nodes exist) despite neither genuinely being able to borrow — user chose to seed `margin_capable` to exactly preserve current behavior (True for brokerage/roth/ira/soxl_ira, False only for sep) over matching real-world capability or redesigning the gate to be cash-aware (stays a separate, already-deferred idea — reopens the unsolved skim-reserve-cash-ambiguity/concurrent-reservation problems).

**Process**: 2 rounds of pre-implementation Opus plan review (caught a wrong `margin_capable=False for roth` seed value before it shipped — roth's real `account_type` had itself already been corrected `"cash"`→`"margin"` earlier the same session as a small standalone fix reflecting the genuine real-world account change, not a refactor side effect; missing `.items()/.keys()/__contains__` dict overrides; a 7-vs-11-table count error; a `monkeypatch.setitem` test hazard), then the required paired post-implementation review (independent-cold + contextual) which found 1 HIGH (two governing comments self-contradicting about whether roth's margin_capable=True was "preserved" or changed — corrected to state it plainly) + 3 MEDIUM (a non-atomic `clear()`-then-repopulate race in the lazy `ACCOUNTS` cache across the daemon's poll-loop/Slack-handler threads, fixed via a lock around the whole check-and-reload decision; the new invariant going permanently red on any future alias retirement, fixed via the live-vs-historical table split; a `RuntimeError` that could in principle escape a `.get()`-shaped call site, checked and found already-safe at the one call site inside real order-placement flow) + 2 LOW (leaked sqlite connections, a dead unused `id` column — both fixed).

**Real live DB migrated**: `cache/live/trading_live.db` itself (not just a throwaway copy) was migrated this session — daemon confirmed not running, backed up first, applied `ensure_tables()`, verified purely additive (table count 26→27, zero row-count deltas on any pre-existing table, `PRAGMA integrity_check` clean). The full suite surfaced 26/764 failures this way (several tests read `schwab_safety.ACCOUNTS` directly against the real default `DB_PATH` with no isolating fixture), every one traced to tests hardcoding `'roth'` as "the cash-typed/non-margin-capable example account" (true pre-session, false after roth's real change) — fixed by switching those specific tests to `'sep'`, confirmed by the contextual review as legitimate, not gamed.

**Verification**: 764/764 full suite, `scripts/live_sim_harness.py` 7/7, `signals_invariants.py` zero violations against the real live DB — all post-fix. `docs/design.md` and `docs/deep_backlog.md` updated with full detail; the older "GDXU/DFEN/KORU need to move to a new Roth account" backlog item's account-side blocker is now resolved (the node migration itself is still open, separate work).

**Not done, deliberately out of scope**: renaming any alias, a surrogate-ID migration, the cash-aware add-on redesign.

## 2026-08-12 (late night) — Fixed the real `brokerage` leverage-gap (core cash + add-on buying power); found and fixed a real live-money bug in the fix itself via paired Opus review; `starting_notional_override` lever built; `node_candidate_trace.py` gained a real params diff

**Core-cash gap closed**: `schwab_client.get_account_balance` now prefers real settled `cashBalance` over the margin-inclusive `availableFunds` -- confirmed via a real API query against all 4 accounts that they're numerically identical today (safe, behavior-preserving), closing the "ordinary BUY could silently draw on margin" gap that had bounded `brokerage.trading_enabled=False` since 2026-07-23.

**Add-on buying-power gap closed, but not on the first try.** Built `get_leveraged_buying_power(account, ticker)` = `equity/margin_req(ticker)` (50%/75% by real leverage factor, confirmed against real Schwab data) to replace the raw `buyingPower` field, which is a blanket 50%-requirement number that overstates real capacity for a genuine 3x fund. Wired into `schwab_safety.check_order`'s `is_addon_leg` branch. **A required paired Opus review (independent-cold + contextual) caught a real, currently-live bug before it could bite**: the formula computes GROSS theoretical capacity (never nets out capital already deployed in open positions) and assumes real 2x/3x borrowing exists wherever `margin_capable=True` -- which is seeded True on `soxl_ira` (a limited-margin IRA with 7 real live `addon_enabled` nodes today) only to preserve an unrelated old gate's behavior, not because it can genuinely borrow. Confirmed live: `soxl_ira`'s real `buyingPower == cashBalance` exactly (zero real leverage), but the unclamped formula would have reported $20,073.76 instead of the real $9,075.38. **Fixed by clamping**: `get_leveraged_buying_power` now returns `min(equity/margin_req, Schwab's raw buyingPower field)` -- Schwab's own real-time number already nets out committed capital and correctly reflects zero leverage on a non-margin account, so the clamp can only ever tighten the raw figure for a genuine 3x fund, never loosen it beyond real availability. The same review also caught `get_account_margin_requirement` missing `abs()` on `fundLeverageFactor` -- inverse funds report a negative factor (confirmed live: YANG=-300.0, ERY=-200.0, SH=-100.0), so a real 3x inverse fund (YANG, a live `addon_enabled` node) was silently misbucketed at 50% instead of 75%. Both fixed, 11 new/updated tests, re-verified live end-to-end against the real `brokerage` account post-fix.

**Real, unmonitored live order testing against `brokerage`** (market closed, zero fill risk) directly answered a user pushback ("I don't believe the $40k buying power is real") -- confirmed Schwab genuinely grants ~$40k on the $20k-equity account, and separately discovered Schwab's real order acceptance is a TWO-STAGE process (immediate "accepted" admission, then an async risk-check that can reject minutes later, surfaced via `get_order`'s `statusDescription` field) -- already fully handled by this codebase's existing `_post_order_confirmation` poll (built 2026-07-24 from an earlier real incident with the same shape), so no new code was needed there. Also confirmed the exact "2 orders exceeding shared buying power" scenario hit manually is already correctly guarded in the real order-placement path (`_has_open_buy_order_for_ticker`/`_reserved_other`) -- only reachable by bypassing `schwab_safety` entirely for the manual test, same pattern `scripts/live_sanity_check.py` already uses deliberately.

**`starting_notional_override` lever built**: found while trying to deliberately resize AGQ/ETHU/JNUG's real position sizing that `signals_helpers._last_sale_recovery` only falls back to `starting_notional` when a node has zero real closed trades -- once one exists, sizing permanently compounds off real trade_log proceeds and a later `starting_notional` edit silently has no effect (same root shape as the LABD basis-lock bug, but for growing a position rather than shrinking it to unbuyable). New nullable `watch_list.starting_notional_override` column + `set_starting_notional_override`/`clear_starting_notional_override` (audit-logged, not one-shot) give a real, deliberate override lever. 10 new tests. Real config change applied: AGQ/ETHU/JNUG `starting_notional` $2,000->$6,000 each (plain field sufficed, no override needed -- none had trade history yet).

**`node_candidate_trace.py` gained a real params diff** (window/z/fixed_sl/arm-or-tp/trail_buy/trail_sell/hold/entry_timing against the linked candidate row, flagging MISMATCH inline) -- closes the gap that let GDXU/DFEN/KORU's real z-score mismatch go undetected in an earlier session. Run against the live DB immediately after building: zero mismatches anywhere.

Real `brokerage` account re-verified end-to-end after a concurrent session flipped `trading_enabled=True` mid-session: correct balances, zero open positions, all 7 real test orders from tonight in terminal CANCELED/REJECTED states.

## 2026-08-12 (evening, cont'd) — Paper-vs-backtest divergence investigated end to end; 2 real code bugs found and fixed, both paired-reviewed with 1 real HIGH catch on the first version

**Started from a user question** ("have any paper portfolios traded, how are they doing vs backtest") that surfaced large, alarming divergences via `scripts/paper_vs_backtest_reconcile.py` — enough that the user considered halting live trading over it. Investigated before acting on that, via direct replay of real production code (`compute_buy_signal`) against real historical prices, the kernel's own trace-capable mirror (`simulate_trail_exit_chaos`'s `trace=`), and the real verbose poll log (`logs/active_signals_verbose.log`).

**4 causes found, zero in real live-execution code:**
1. **Reconciliation-tool bug**: wrong node-config selection (`load_nodes()`'s `MIN(id)`/`state='paper'` heuristic broke on promoted/duplicate nodes) — fixed via `resolve_live_track_nodes_by_activity()`, resolving by which `wl_id` actually has real trade history.
2. **Reconciliation-tool bug**: unbounded full-history backtest replay caused a cold-start artifact (confirmed real for KORU/YANG, no-op for HIBL/USD/SOXL) — fixed via `get_trades_and_bars_since(node, sim_start)`, slicing the simulator's position-tracking loop to start flat at the node's own `added_at`.
3. **Real `paper_trading.py` bug**: `update_paper_buys()` priced its trailing-buy fill tracking off `_current_price()` (cached hourly bar, refreshed only on the background collector's own schedule) instead of a live tick — traced via the real poll log to SOXL's 2026-07-27 gap-up-then-crash: `_current_price` returned the identical $140.08 for 29 straight minutes right after the gap, missing the real $140.06 Open fill entirely and instead bounce-filling at $121.615 two hours later. Fixed by extracting `signals_compute._live_tick_price()` (factored out of `compute_buy_signal`'s existing inline fetch) and upgrading to it after `_current_price`'s staleness gate passes.
4. **Real operational history, not a bug**: all 10 v5 live-track nodes were flipped to `mode='live'` 2026-07-23 12:56→2026-07-25 07:31 (documented "real-account test day") — paper trading wasn't running for ~42.5h, explaining part of HIBL/USD/SOXL's divergence (missed/delayed signal detection, on top of #3 for SOXL specifically).

**Paired Opus review (independent-cold + contextual)** on the fix diff found and fixed 1 real HIGH + 3 MEDIUM before landing: the live-tick upgrade wasn't gated against `paper_role='daily_sync'` nodes, silently breaking the daily-track experiment's deliberate price-source isolation (11 real daily-track TrailingBoth nodes exist, none had filled yet — would have corrupted the first one); no bound on a single bad extended-hours print ratcheting `running_low` down (fixed by reusing `signals_notify`'s existing `MAX_RUNNING_LOW_DROP_PCT`, moved to `signals_helpers.py` to avoid a circular import); `sim_start`'s UTC-vs-naive-ET timezone mismatch (the two reviewers disagreed on this one — resolved by direct DB verification, cold review was right, contextual review had a factual error); and `resolve_live_track_nodes_by_activity` making genuinely-inactive nodes (DPST/GDXU/NUGT) vanish from the report instead of showing "paper never traded" explicitly.

**Verification**: full suite 811/811 (was 810/811 immediately after the review fixes — one test referenced the old private `signals_notify._MAX_RUNNING_LOW_DROP_PCT` name directly, updated to the new shared-constant name). `scripts/live_sim_harness.py` 7/7. `signals_invariants.py` clean. No `active_signals.py`/`strategies.py`/`backtester.py` changes this session. No new `coverage_events`/`scenario_key` call sites — Accountability Grid and truth tables (`test_entry_abandon_truth_table.py`, `test_fake_broker_overlay_truth_table_scenario.py`) unaffected, confirmed by inspection (this session only changes which price value feeds an existing fill-check, not any reachable-state/transition).

**Full detail**: `docs/research_log.md`'s 2026-08-12 (evening) entry; `docs/deep_backlog.md`'s two matching entries.

**Concurrent session note**: `config.json` and `docs/backlog_cache.md` had unrelated uncommitted changes from a parallel session throughout (a sweep hyperparameter grid change, 2 new backlog items) — left untouched, not included in this session's commit.

**Real bug found and backlogged, HIGH — no same-bar re-entry cooldown**: traced a real RETL (`soxl_ira`) TIME exit + trailing-buy re-entry ~1 minute apart (exit 09:30:52 ET, new order 09:31:54 ET, both real, confirmed via broker order log). Root-caused: `active_signals.py`'s exit-scan (`_scan_pinned_exit_arm`, pinned to all 7 hourly bar boundaries) and entry-scan (4 of those 7, or a node's own `entry_timing='open_check'` window) are fully independent, no coordination. The only re-buy guard (`same_day_block`) is same-*day*, not same-*bar*, and is skipped for margin accounts. Checked the backtest kernel directly (`_simulate_trail_both`, `backtester.py:731`): its single per-bar `if in_trade: ... elif waiting: ... else: <entry check>` structure enforces a minimum one-bar gap between any exit and the next entry-check — live has no equivalent gap. Confirmed via cached-data math that with exactly 7 bars/day, this isn't RETL-specific: any real node using `entry_timing='open_check'` + a multiple-of-7 `max_hold_hours` (the real-node convention) would show the same structural gap if it ever reaches a full-hold TIME exit. Scheduled fix (design agreed, not built): a cooldown requiring a bar strictly newer than the node's last exit bar before allowing a fresh entry check, matching the kernel's `i+1` semantics — not a fixed time window. `trade_log.exit_bar_time` column already exists in schema but is only populated by `paper_trading.py`, never the real exit path — needs wiring for real exits too.

## 2026-08-14 — Portfolio construction prototype rebuilt from scratch after original file lost; 5 real bugs found and fixed in candidate-node tooling (1 already-live, self-caused, corrected same session)

Rebuilt a lost mobaxterm portfolio-selection spreadsheet (~3+ hours of original work, no recoverable backup) from `output/candidate_full_review_20260809_192051.xlsx`, walking through the user's real process step by step (documented in full in `docs/portfolio_construction_notes.md`): Keys section (node_id→c_id, ticker, account, pick, comment, liquidity, account_mod, trades_per_year, target_cagr formula, trades, years, strategy_cagr_pct), tax/structural tagging (K1/ETN/Clean, Commodity/Treasury/Crypto/<20/Clean), leverage_factor parsing, 3-way cliff-safety labels, addon/drought CAGR conversion, column grouping, conditional highlighting (green=tranche OK, yellow=account_mod's actual pick, light-red=core baseline), and a real 4-phase process (revenue organization → node/account selection → other filters → circle back).

**Real, persistent capability built** (the actual point, beyond the one-off spreadsheet): `account_mod`/`account` now persist to a new `candidate_nodes.account_mod`/`account` column pair (mirrors the existing `pick`/`comment` pattern) so manual judgment calls survive a rebuild instead of only living in an Excel file. Seeded the 10 real live tickers' `account_mod` from their actual historical `watch_list_candidate_link` role (core/drought/add_on/overlay), not auto-computed.

**Real data-integrity gap found and closed**: none of the 10 real live candidate_nodes had a `sweep_run_id`, so there was no way to tell from the DB whether a stored `robust_alpha` reflected current data or a stale pre-backfill window. Confirmed real: 6 of 10 tickers (JNUG/DFEN/GDXU/ETHU/NUGT/SOXS) had `years=1.11` at actual decision time (pulled from real old snapshot evidence) vs ~2.9-3+ years available today. Added `robust_alpha_computed_at`/`years_at_computation`/`data_start`/`data_end` to `candidate_nodes`; backfilled `robust_alpha_computed_at` for 340/341 rows via a reliable direct join to `backtest_cache.run_timestamp` (no guessing); explicitly left `data_start`/`data_end` NULL for old rows rather than fabricate them.

**Paired Opus review (independent-cold + contextual) of the resulting tooling diff found 3 real bugs, one already causing live damage**, all fixed and verified (8/8 relevant tests pass):
1. **HIGH, already live**: the first version of the provenance-stamping code stamped `datetime.now()` unconditionally on every touch, fabricating "computed today" on rows actually computed weeks earlier -- confirmed it had already corrupted 24 real `candidate_nodes` rows (including AGQ/SOXL/KORU/DPST) within this session. Fixed to thread the real `backtest_cache.run_timestamp` through instead, and to only trust today's real CSV bounds for `data_start`/`data_end` when the underlying computation genuinely happened today. All 24 corrupted rows restored to honest values.
2. **HIGH**: `ensure_candidate_nodes_table()` was never given migration guards for the new columns -- any fresh DB (test DB, clone, another machine) crashed on first insert. Fixed, reproduced test failure confirmed resolved.
3. **MEDIUM**: the tie-break fix for `best_row()`/`top_safe_nodes.best_safe_node()` (added earlier same session after an exact-alpha-tie bug on ETHU let the two independently-implemented node-selection functions silently disagree) was incomplete -- 34-69 real ticker groups (including live-linked DPST/KORU) still tied on all 4 original tie-break keys. Extended to a genuine total order on both sides; verified DPST now agrees exactly between the two functions.

**Also fixed along the way**: `run_overlay_shim.py` was hardcoded to `version="v5"`, silently using stale pre-backfill data for tickers with newer `v5.1` data (found live on ETHU: stale robust_alpha=180.9 vs real current 320.0) -- now auto-resolves per ticker, same convention `candidate_full_review.py` already uses. `resolve_version()` moved from `candidate_summary_report.py` to `locate_best_node.py` to fix a real circular import this surfaced. Added `run_overlay_shim.py --node-id` (backed by new `node_from_candidate_id()`) so a caller can target an exact report row instead of re-deriving "best" independently -- confirmed the two selection functions can legitimately disagree by design (different selection philosophies), not just via bugs.

**New tools built**: `scripts/sweep_drought_confirm_days.py` (real per-ticker confirm_days optimizer -- most tickers' drought numbers were running on a generic unvalidated confirm_days=10, not tuned). `scripts/run_1y_window_sweep.sh` (safe CSV-truncate-and-restore pattern for a real trailing-window sweep, since the kernel has no native date-window parameter -- not run this session, built and ready).

**Side investigation**: JNUG's `force_same_day_block=1` (live since 2026-08-11) checked against its exact real node config -- full-history absolute cost is real and large (2,374.7% unblocked vs 590.7% blocked compounded return over 2.92yr), but the trailing-1.11yr window (matching the original decision's own methodology) still favors blocking (562.6% vs 415.4%), though the effect is fading within that window, not improving (5-way split showed no clean trend, too few trades per slice to call it either way). **User's decision: leave it on, kill after the first real live trade closes under it.**

Full detail: `docs/portfolio_construction_notes.md` (46+ numbered items, phase-by-phase). All code changes currently uncommitted, scoped to: `scripts/locate_best_node.py`, `scripts/run_overlay_shim.py`, `scripts/top_safe_nodes.py`, `scripts/candidate_summary_report.py`, plus new `scripts/build_portfolio_prototype.py`, `scripts/sweep_drought_confirm_days.py`, `scripts/run_1y_window_sweep.sh`, `docs/portfolio_construction_notes.md` -- deliberately does NOT include `scripts/evening_status.py`/`scripts/watch_evening_status.sh`, which are a concurrent session's in-flight work.
